# pd-components v0.9.0

> Light-DOM web components for rich single-file HTML planning documents.
> One classic script tag, no build step, works from file:// pages. The HTML
> source is the canonical data — write it like markup, the components render
> it into an interactive doc.

Current release: `pd-v0.9.0`. Pin every generated doc to this exact tag (jsDelivr
caches tags immutably, so old docs never change appearance under the reader).

## Boilerplate

Every doc starts with exactly this head. Use a CLASSIC script tag (not
type="module" — module scripts are CORS-blocked when the file is opened via
file://).

```html
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>NNN: Doc title</title>
  <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@tailwindcss/browser@4"></script>
  <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/mistakenot/skills@pd-v0.9.0/pd-components/dist/pd.min.js" defer></script>
</head>
<body>
  <!-- AI: When a PR is created for this work, update pr="pending" below with the PR URL -->
  <pd-doc title="NNN: Doc title" status="draft" pr="pending" generated="YYYY-MM-DD">
    ...
  </pd-doc>
</body>
</html>
```

Tailwind is optional — include it only if the doc has freeform/wireframe
content. pd-* components style themselves.

## Authoring rules

- **Use `<md>` for prose content** (paragraphs, lists, links, inline code,
  tables). Agents read and generate markdown natively at lower token cost than
  HTML. Reserve raw HTML for pd-* structural elements and Tailwind wireframe
  layouts.
- Structure lives in pd-* elements and ids, never in utility-class div soup.
  Tailwind classes belong ONLY inside freeform/wireframe content.
- Give every pd-section a stable, kebab-case id. Threads and deep links anchor
  to these ids; content can then be freely rewritten without orphaning its
  discussion.
- **Prefer structured attributes over prose.** Anything a reader would scan,
  count, or cross-reference — phase order, file changes, coverage, dependencies
  — belongs in attributes, not sentences. The components derive visual summaries
  (pd-scope, pd-dag, pd-trace), cross-highlighting, and consistency checks from
  those attributes for free. Keep prose for the *why*; put the *what* in markup.
- **Visual-first sections.** Open a section with its diagram/graph/matrix, then
  put the explanation in a `summary=` (auto-collapsed) or `<pd-collapse>`. Don't
  describe in prose what an attribute-driven component already shows.
- Content is edited in place; threads are APPEND-ONLY. Never delete or rewrite
  an existing pd-comment — append a new one and update the thread's status
  attribute. Resolved threads collapse automatically in the UI; the history
  stays in the file.
- Place a pd-thread in the source directly after the element it discusses, and
  set anchor to that element's id (or a pd-file's path).
- doc status attribute — the lifecycle stage, driving the status banner (see
  pd-doc). Four stages, each set at a defined point in the workflow:
  - draft — default when the doc is first created
  - pending — set when the plan is committed and awaiting execution
  - executing — set when work is dispatched to a worker
  - complete — set by the worker once the PR is done
  You never set "blocked": the banner shows blocked (red) automatically whenever
  any comment thread is unresolved, overriding whatever stage is set.

## Components

### <pd-doc title status pr generated next-prompt>
Document shell: status banner, header, PR link bar, tab navigation (when it
contains pd-tab children), floating "Copy for agent" bar for pending comments,
provenance footer. Direct children: either pd-tab elements, or sections directly.

status banner — a full-width bar across the top reflecting the lifecycle stage
(the status attribute): draft (grey), pending (blue), executing (animated
amber), complete (green). Any unresolved comment thread overrides this to a red
"Blocked — N open comment threads" bar (click to jump to the first open thread),
so an in-progress doc with open review automatically reads as blocked. Set an
accurate status; the blocked override is derived from thread state.

pr: "pending" shows a muted placeholder; a URL (e.g.
"https://github.com/org/repo/pull/42") renders a clickable badge. Omit entirely
if no PR tracking is needed. When the executor opens a PR, it should update
pr="pending" to the actual URL.

next-prompt: optional. The prompt/command a human runs to advance this doc to
its NEXT workflow stage once they're satisfied with the current one — e.g. after
reviewing the Requirements tab, the next prompt is the solution step. Rendered as
a prominent "Next step" banner at the top of the doc with a copy-to-clipboard
button, so the reviewer can approve and push to the next stage in one click. It's
a hint, not an action: the doc author fills it in; the human stays the gate (the
banner dims automatically while any thread/question is open, since the next step
isn't actionable until the doc is unblocked). Set it to the exact thing the human
should paste — usually a slash command with the task id, e.g.
next-prompt="/new-solution 042". Clear or update it when the stage changes; omit
it on terminal docs (nothing comes next) or one-off docs with no pipeline.

### <pd-tab name>
One page of a tabbed doc. Tab buttons show a badge with the count of open
threads inside. Deep links: #tab:Name, or any #element-id inside the tab.

```html
<pd-tab name="Solution"> ...sections... </pd-tab>
```

Tab roles (a deliberate audience split — follow it):
- **Solution = the end state** once the work is done. Human-consumed: someone
  checking the final outcome. The file-change tree (pd-files), API outlines,
  and final code snippets belong here.
- **Plan = the recipe** to get there. Agent-consumed: planning/executing. Keep
  it self-sufficient (pd-phase already lists its files inline).

### <pd-section id title summary>
Titled section with anchor link and a "+ comment" button (reviewers queue
comments in the browser). Body is `<md>` blocks and pd-* elements.

summary: optional one-line scan summary. When present, the summary shows
always-visible and the section body collapses into a "Details" disclosure
(add `open` to expand by default). The full body stays in the DOM for agents —
this is the human skim layer, not a content cut. Use it on prose-heavy sections.

```html
<pd-section id="approach" title="Approach">
  <md><script type="text/plain">
Token-bucket limiter as gateway middleware, backed by Redis.
Bursts up to bucket size are allowed; sustained rate is capped at the refill rate.
  </script></md>
</pd-section>
```

### <md>
Client-side markdown block. Use for prose content inside pd-* containers —
paragraphs, lists, inline code, links, tables. Replaces verbose HTML (`<p>`,
`<ul><li>`, `<code>`, `<a href>`) with compact markdown, rendered by marked
(loaded from CDN on demand — no extra script tag needed).

Use `<md>` for: section bodies, phase descriptions, AC criteria, notes —
anything that would otherwise be `<p>`, `<ul>`, `<table>`, `<a>`, or inline
`<code>`.

Keep raw HTML for: pd-* components (pd-mermaid, pd-code, pd-files, etc.),
wireframe layouts (Tailwind), content requiring HTML attributes.

**Always wrap `<md>` content in `<script type="text/plain">`** to prevent the
browser's HTML parser from interpreting angle brackets as tags. Without the
wrapper, markdown containing `<textarea>`, `<script>`, `<style>`, or any HTML
tag name in backtick-code will break the document structure — the parser treats
them as real HTML elements before marked ever runs.

```html
<pd-section id="limits" title="Rate limits">
  <md><script type="text/plain">
Per-client rate limiting at the gateway, backed by Redis:

- **Free plan**: 100 req/min
- **Partner plan**: 1000 req/min
- Exceeding the limit returns `429` with a `Retry-After` header
- Custom props via a `<textarea>` JSON editor

See the [design doc](https://example.com/design) for background.
  </script></md>
</pd-section>
```

### <pd-thread anchor status title priority> / <pd-comment by>
Append-only review thread. status: unresolved (default) | resolved | rejected.
priority: p1 (blocking) | p2 (important) | p3 (minor). by: review | author |
a person's name. Open threads render a reply box; closed ones collapse.

```html
<pd-thread anchor="approach" status="resolved" priority="p2" title="Why not sliding window?">
  <pd-comment by="review">Token bucket allows bursts — is that acceptable for the API tier?</pd-comment>
  <pd-comment by="author">Yes — bursts up to bucket size are within SLA; documented in the Approach section.</pd-comment>
</pd-thread>
```

### <pd-question id status priority for title recommendedAnswer> / <pd-answer by>
A question the HUMAN must answer before the plan can proceed — the reverse of a
pd-thread (there the human reviews you; here you block on the human). Use it
whenever you hit a decision you cannot resolve from the requirements, the code,
or a sensible default — don't bury it in prose or guess. status: open (default)
| answered. priority: p1 (blocking) | p2 (important) | p3 (minor). for: who
should answer (optional). Give each a stable id so links and tooling can anchor
to it. The question prose is the body; the human's answer arrives via the
"Copy for agent" paste-back as an ANSWER item — merge it as a <pd-answer
by="…"> child and set status="answered".

recommendedAnswer (optional): YOUR suggested answer — what you'd do absent a
human ruling. Add it whenever you have a defensible lean, so the human can
rubber-stamp (it pre-fills the answer box — one click) or override instead of
starting cold. It is a suggestion, NOT an answer: it does NOT close the gate or
clear the linter; only a <pd-answer> + status="answered" does. Prefer a question
WITH a recommendedAnswer over silently guessing — you still surface the decision,
you just make it cheap to confirm.

Open questions are a gate, not chatter: while any exist the doc's status bar
shows "blocked", and the headless linter reports them (code "open-question",
non-zero exit) so an automated step won't run past them. They are NOT a defect
you fix — surface them to the human and wait for the answer.

```html
<pd-question id="Q-1" status="open" priority="p1" for="product"
             title="Which tier do internal services use?"
             recommendedAnswer="Separate unlimited tier, keyed by service id — safest default.">
  Internal callers hit the same gateway. Do they share the public tier's bucket,
  or get a separate unlimited tier? This changes how the limiter keys clients.
</pd-question>

<!-- once answered: -->
<pd-question id="Q-1" status="answered" priority="p1" for="product"
             title="Which tier do internal services use?"
             recommendedAnswer="Separate unlimited tier, keyed by service id — safest default.">
  Internal callers hit the same gateway. Do they share the public tier's bucket,
  or get a separate unlimited tier? This changes how the limiter keys clients.
  <pd-answer by="charlie">Separate unlimited tier; key by service identity.</pd-answer>
</pd-question>
```

### <pd-files> / <pd-file path change>
File-change list. Write flat pd-file children (cheap to append); renders as a
collapsible tree with +/~/− markers, per-file notes, and open-thread badges
for threads whose anchor equals the file path. change: add | edit | delete.

```html
<pd-files>
  <pd-file path="src/gateway/limiter.ts" change="add">Token bucket implementation</pd-file>
  <pd-file path="src/gateway/index.ts" change="edit">Wire limiter into request pipeline</pd-file>
  <pd-file path="src/legacy/throttle.ts" change="delete">Superseded</pd-file>
</pd-files>
```

### <pd-stepper> / <pd-phase n title files status depends-on>
Clickable, non-linear plan walkthrough. Selecting a phase shows its body and
highlights its files (comma-separated paths matching pd-file paths) in every
pd-files on the page. status: done | active | todo. Arrow keys navigate.

depends-on: comma-separated phase numbers this phase must follow. Drives the
pd-dag graph and conflict detection. Set it whenever an ordering actually
exists — it's the structured data the graph and the linter read.

Selection is shared: clicking a phase here, clicking its node in pd-dag, or
keyboard-focusing that node all select the same phase everywhere (stepper, dag,
and the file tree highlight stay in sync). No wiring needed — it's automatic.

```html
<pd-stepper>
  <pd-phase n="1" title="Limiter core" files="src/gateway/limiter.ts" status="done">
    <md><script type="text/plain">Implement and unit-test the bucket…</script></md>
  </pd-phase>
  <pd-phase n="2" title="Gateway wiring" files="src/gateway/index.ts" status="active" depends-on="1">
    <md><script type="text/plain">Apply per-route config…</script></md>
  </pd-phase>
</pd-stepper>
```

### <pd-mermaid caption>
Renders mermaid source (bundled beautiful-mermaid — no extra fetch, follows
light/dark mode). Supported types: flowchart/graph, sequenceDiagram,
stateDiagram(-v2), classDiagram, erDiagram, xychart-beta. Do NOT use other
types (gantt, pie, mindmap…) — they fall back to a source-code block. Put the
mermaid source as plain text content; indentation is fine.

```html
<pd-mermaid caption="Request path">
flowchart LR
  C[Client] --> G[Gateway] --> S[Service]
</pd-mermaid>
```

### <pd-code lang path lines highlight caption>
Syntax-highlighted snippet (highlight.js bundled — no extra fetch). lang:
go|ts|js|python|json|bash|yaml|sql|rust|diff (others auto-detect). path: shows
a filename header + copy button. lines: boolean, adds line numbers. highlight:
emphasize line ranges, e.g. "2-3,7". Put the code as the element's text
content. If the code contains <, >, or &, wrap it in a nested
<script type="text/plain"> to avoid HTML-escaping.

```html
<pd-code lang="go" path="internal/events/log.go" lines highlight="3-4" caption="Append under flock">
func AppendEvent(dir string, ev Event) error {
	f, _ := os.OpenFile(shard(dir), os.O_RDWR|os.O_CREATE, 0o644)
	flock(f, LOCK_EX)
	ev.Seq = lastSeq(f) + 1
	return writeLine(f, ev)
}
</pd-code>
```

### <pd-api kind name lang path caption> / <pd-member kind sig>
Token-efficient outline of a code symbol — the public surface only
(signatures + doc comments, no bodies). Generic by design: `kind` on the
container (class|struct|interface|module|enum|routes|schema|…) and on each
member (constructor|method|field|…) are free-form labels rendered as badges,
so the same component outlines a Go struct, a TS class, a REST route table, or
a SQL schema. Member signature goes in the `sig` attribute; the doc comment is
the member's text content. Signatures are syntax-highlighted with `lang`.
Prefer this over a full pd-code dump when the reader only needs the API shape.

```html
<pd-api kind="struct" name="loop.Service" lang="go" path="internal/loop/service.go" caption="Agent-facing state machine">
  <pd-member kind="constructor" sig="NewService(log *events.Log, pb *rules.Playbook) *Service">Binds the loop to the canonical log and folded snapshot.</pd-member>
  <pd-member kind="method" sig="Retrieve(intent string, domains []string, limit int) ([]Predicate, error)">Match + mint rt-ids; append one retrieval event; predicates only.</pd-member>
  <pd-member kind="field" sig="Lookback time.Duration">No-session gate fallback window (default 24h).</pd-member>
</pd-api>
```

### <pd-unit kind name extends implements lang path caption> / <pd-dep name type access> / <pd-fn sig> / <pd-prop sig>
Opinionated TypeScript code-unit outline, organised around the three things a
reviewer checks first: (1) identity — `kind` (class|service|interface|abstract
class|…), `name`, and `extends`/`implements` lineage; (2) constructor
dependencies — one `<pd-dep>` per injected dependency (`name`, `type`, optional
`access` like `private readonly`); (3) public surface — `<pd-fn>` methods and
`<pd-prop>` properties, signature in `sig`, doc comment as text content. Bodies
are omitted by design — the rest is inferable. Types/signatures are
syntax-highlighted as TypeScript (override with `lang`). Prefer pd-unit over
pd-api when outlining a TS class and the constructor dependencies matter to the
reader; use pd-api for a language-agnostic flat symbol dump.

`path` doubles as a join key: selecting a phase in pd-stepper (or pd-dag /
pd-ac) highlights every pd-unit whose `path` is in that phase's `files` list,
the same way pd-files rows light up. Give a unit the same path string the phase
uses to wire the two together — no extra attribute needed.

```html
<pd-unit kind="service" name="RateLimiter" implements="Limiter" path="src/limit/rate-limiter.ts" caption="Sliding-window limiter behind the gateway 429s.">
  <pd-dep name="redis" type="RedisClient" access="private readonly">Shared pool; one round-trip per check.</pd-dep>
  <pd-dep name="clock" type="Clock" access="private readonly">Wall-clock, faked in tests.</pd-dep>
  <pd-fn sig="allow(key: string): Promise<boolean>">True if the key is under budget for the window.</pd-fn>
  <pd-fn sig="reset(key: string): Promise<void>">Clears a key's window — admin/test escape hatch.</pd-fn>
  <pd-prop sig="readonly windowMs: number">Window length, exposed for the Retry-After header.</pd-prop>
</pd-unit>
```

### <pd-cli id title caption> / <pd-cmd note status> / <pd-out>
Terminal transcript showing the FINAL SHAPE of a dev tool / CLI / API from the
user's point of view — the commands they run and the output they get back. This
is the clearest way to state "what does success look like" for a command-line
product. Epic-altitude: describe the experience, never the files behind it.

pd-cmd is one command line; `note` renders as a dimmed inline `# comment`.
pd-out is the output for the preceding command(s), always dimmed. `status` on a
pd-cmd (done|active|todo) tints the line so a reader sees what works today vs
what is still coming — progress read in user-visible capability, not files. If a
command or output contains <, >, or &, wrap its text in a nested
<script type="text/plain">.

```html
<pd-cli title="zsh — authoring a skill" caption="The one-command author→install loop">
  <pd-cmd note="scaffold from a description" status="done">npx skills new my-skill</pd-cmd>
  <pd-out>✓ scaffolded src/my-skill/SKILL.md</pd-out>
  <pd-cmd note="compile + install into every agent" status="active">make install</pd-cmd>
  <pd-out>✓ installed: claude-code, codex</pd-out>
</pd-cli>
```

Give the transcript an `id` to join the epic graph (see pd-task): a task's
delivers= references it, so selecting the transcript shows which tasks deliver
it, and selecting one of those tasks lights it up.

### <pd-journey id title outcome caption> / <pd-leg actor action status>
User journey at epic altitude: the legs a user travels to reach an outcome, told
from their point of view, rendered as a connected flow. The app analogue of
pd-cli — use it when the product is a service/UI rather than a CLI. Light-touch:
no screens, no files, no implementation. Legs auto-number; `outcome` caps the
flow with the user-visible result. `status` on a leg (done|active|todo) tints it
so the reader sees how much of the journey is real today vs still coming. An
optional `id` joins the epic graph the same way pd-cli's does (tasks deliver= it).

```html
<pd-journey id="J1" title="Author → shipped feature" outcome="merged PR, no manual coding">
  <pd-leg actor="author" action="describes the feature" status="done">requirements appear</pd-leg>
  <pd-leg actor="agent" action="plans → executes" status="active">a PR opens</pd-leg>
  <pd-leg actor="author" action="reviews &amp; merges" status="todo">feedback addressed</pd-leg>
</pd-journey>
```

### <pd-guardrail id kind metric title>
A constraint every task in an epic inherits — the invariants the initiative must
preserve. `kind`: functional (default) | performance | security | cost | a11y |
reliability | compat | privacy | operability | scalability — non-functional kinds
are grouped apart by pd-outcome. `metric`: optional measurable target (e.g. "p99
< 200ms"). It's a join-key, not a design: a task references its `id` via honors=,
so selecting a guard rail shows its blast radius (every task bound by it), and
pd-outcome flags any rail no task honors. Body is the constraint statement.

```html
<pd-guardrail id="G1" kind="performance" metric="p99 < 200ms" title="Stays within budget under load">
  <md><script type="text/plain">Sustained rate under the partner-tier ceiling; bursts shed, not queued.</script></md>
</pd-guardrail>
```

### <pd-task id title status depends-on delivers honors deployable gated href>
One unit of an epic's decomposition — NOT a phase: no files, no steps. It carries
only what the epic tracks. `status`: todo|active|done. `depends-on`: other task
ids it builds on (drives pd-breakdown). `delivers`: journey/cli ids it advances.
`honors`: guard-rail ids it must respect. `deployable`: independently shippable.
`gated`: ships behind a feature flag. `href`: link to its plan.html once planned.
Selecting a task lights up what it delivers and honors. Body is a one-line intent.

```html
<pd-task id="T1" title="Token-bucket limiter" status="done" deployable
         delivers="J1" honors="G1,G2" href="docs/tasks/021-rate-limit/plan.html">
  <md><script type="text/plain">The limiter core behind the gateway 429s.</script></md>
</pd-task>
```

### <pd-breakdown caption>
Dependency DAG over every pd-task, fully derived from depends-on — the deployment
sequence at a glance (roots left, each column builds on the last). Clicking a node
selects that task everywhere (same as clicking its card). Zero authoring beyond
the cards. Place it at the top of the breakdown section.

```html
<pd-breakdown caption="Build order"></pd-breakdown>
```

### <pd-outcome>
The epic-altitude scan strip, fully derived — no attributes. The analogue of
pd-scope: counts journeys (pd-journey + pd-cli), guard rails (functional vs
non-functional), and tasks (by status, how many deployable), and flags coverage
gaps — a guard rail no task honors, a journey/cli (with an id) no task delivers.
Drop one at the top of the Vision tab.

```html
<pd-outcome></pd-outcome>
```

### <pd-ac id title phases tests open>
Acceptance-criteria card with traceability chips. phases: comma-separated
phase numbers covering it; tests: comma-separated test files.

**Check-free cards (every already-authored doc) are unchanged:** a pd-ac with no
pd-ac-check-* child renders exactly as before — head chips, body visible, no
pill, no disclosure, whole-card click dispatches `pd:phase-selected`.

**With ≥1 pd-ac-check-* child the card renders its completion contract:**

- **Rollup pill + count.** The head gains a `.pd-ac-pill` coloured by the rolled-
  up status plus an `n/m checks passing` count (m = total checks, n = checks
  authored `status="proved"`). The AC rolls up `proved` only when EVERY check is
  `proved`; otherwise the worst-severity status present, ordered
  `contradicted ≻ missing ≻ weak ≻ pending ≻ proved` (absent/unknown → pending).
  Colour: `proved`→green · `contradicted`→red · `weak`/`missing`→amber ·
  `pending`→grey (reuses the existing ok/bad/warn/neutral vars).
- **Two-level progressive disclosure (AC → checks → evidence).** The card is
  collapsed by default behind a native `<details>` whose summary is the AC head.
  Expanding reveals the Given/When/Then body and one row per check (status glyph
  + a `type · key-attr` label). A check carrying a `<pd-ac-evidence>` child
  reveals its captured evidence (+ a muted commit/dirty/at last-run stamp) at a
  second disclosure level. Author evidence as a direct child of the check:
  `<pd-ac-check-* …><pd-ac-evidence>…captured output…</pd-ac-evidence></…>`.
- **Auto-open.** A card whose rollup is `contradicted` renders expanded
  automatically; `<pd-ac open>` pins it open explicitly.
- **Click model.** The header/summary toggles the disclosure; only the **phase
  chips** (not the whole card) fire the `pd:phase-selected` reverse-traceability
  trigger. (Check-free cards keep the old whole-card click.)
- Purely additive: rollup/disclosure engage only when checks are present; the
  rollup is over AUTHORED/written-back status — it executes nothing.

```html
<pd-ac id="AC-1" title="Requests over the limit get 429" phases="1,2" tests="e2e/rate-limit.spec.ts">
  <md><script type="text/plain">
- Given a client at its request budget
- When it sends one more request within the window
- Then the gateway responds `429` with a `Retry-After` header
  </script></md>
</pd-ac>
```

### <pd-contract>
Document-level completion banner. Author it (like pd-decisions) where you want
the summary — e.g. just above the acceptance criteria. Fully derived, no
attributes: it scans every pd-ac that carries checks, rolls each up the SAME way
the card does (`rollupContract` over each AC's status), and renders an
`n/m ACs proved` count (m = ACs that carry checks, n = those that rolled up to
`proved`) + a contract-status pill. The contract is `proved` only when EVERY
participating AC is `proved`. Check-free ACs are excluded. It renders
authored/written-back status only — it executes nothing — and a doc with no
pd-contract is unaffected.

```html
<pd-contract></pd-contract>
```

### <pd-ac-check-* family> (pd-ac-check-command / -output / -test / -file-exists / -file-contains)
Five inert checks that nest inside a pd-ac to declare *how* the criterion is
proved (executable completion contract). Each carries only input attributes; the
authored shape is the single source of truth (`src/ac-check-core.js`,
`AC_CHECK_SCHEMA`). The five types and their attributes:

- `pd-ac-check-command run expect-exit` — run a command, assert its exit code
  (`expect-exit` defaults to 0).
- `pd-ac-check-output run matches` — run a command, assert stdout matches the
  `matches` regex.
- `pd-ac-check-test report name suite classname file` — look up a testcase in a
  JUnit XML `report` by portable identity (see contract below).
- `pd-ac-check-file-exists path` — assert `path` exists.
- `pd-ac-check-file-contains path pattern` — assert `path` matches `pattern`.

**test identity contract.** `report` + `name` are the required portable identity;
`suite` / `classname` / `file` are optional qualifiers that narrow the match.
Lookup rule: 0-or-many matches = non-proof, never a pass.

**Behavioural checks (G3).** A check is behavioural when it proves runtime
behaviour rather than static presence: `test`, `output`, and a *negative*
`command` (one with a non-zero `expect-exit`) are behavioural; a plain exit-0
`command`, `file-exists`, and `file-contains` are static gates.

**Reserved write-back shape.** A later phase writes a result back onto each check;
the shape is reserved (frozen) now, unused in this version:
- `status` attribute, vocabulary: `proved` · `contradicted` · `weak` · `missing`
  · `pending`.
- evidence as a reserved **child element** (carries multi-line output), not an
  attribute.
- provenance as reserved attributes: `commit`, `dirty`, `at` (when the write
  happened and against what tree).

**Inert in this version — no status / no rendering yet.** The elements register
and expose a read-only `.check` parse of their own attributes, but add no DOM,
no visual treatment, no status, and no events; the write-back / status fields
above are reserved and not yet written or rendered.

```html
<pd-ac id="AC-1" title="Requests over the limit get 429" phases="1,2" tests="e2e/rate-limit.spec.ts">
  <md><script type="text/plain">
- Given a client at its request budget
- When it sends one more request within the window
- Then the gateway responds `429` with a `Retry-After` header
  </script></md>
  <pd-ac-check-test report="junit.xml" name="returns 429 over budget" classname="RateLimit"></pd-ac-check-test>
  <pd-ac-check-command run="npm run typecheck" expect-exit="0"></pd-ac-check-command>
  <pd-ac-check-output run="curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' localhost/api" matches="429"></pd-ac-check-output>
  <pd-ac-check-file-exists path="src/rate-limit.ts"></pd-ac-check-file-exists>
  <pd-ac-check-file-contains path="src/rate-limit.ts" pattern="Retry-After"></pd-ac-check-file-contains>
</pd-ac>
```

### <pd-scope>
At-a-glance summary strip, fully derived — no attributes, no authoring. Counts
the pd-phase / pd-file / pd-ac / pd-thread elements already in the doc and
renders tiles: phase count + done/active/todo progress bar, file count + add/
edit/delete tally, criteria count + coverage gaps, open-thread count. Drop one
at the top of the first tab for an instant scan-level summary.

```html
<pd-scope></pd-scope>
```

### <pd-dag caption>
Phase dependency graph, fully derived from the pd-phase elements — no
attributes besides an optional caption. Reads depends-on for explicit edges and
auto-detects conflict edges (two phases share a file but neither depends on the
other, so they aren't parallel-safe — drawn dashed + listed). Clicking or
focusing a node selects that phase everywhere (see pd-stepper). Place it in the
Plan tab; it replaces hand-drawn sequence diagrams.

```html
<pd-dag caption="Execution order"></pd-dag>
```

### <pd-trace caption>
Traceability matrix, fully derived from pd-ac. Renders an AC × phase × test
grid from each card's phases and tests attributes; rows missing a phase or a
test are flagged as coverage gaps. No authoring — it reads data already on the
pd-ac cards. Place it in the criteria section.

Interactive both ways: clicking a row (or a pd-ac card) highlights the phases
and files that satisfy that criterion; selecting a phase anywhere highlights the
criteria it covers.

```html
<pd-trace caption="Acceptance coverage"></pd-trace>
```

### <pd-collapse summary>
Ad-hoc disclosure wrapper. Collapsed by default (add `open` to expand); the
summary is the scan line, the body stays in the DOM for agents. Use for long
code, tables, or secondary rationale that isn't a whole section.

```html
<pd-collapse summary="Why token bucket (rationale)">
  <md><script type="text/plain">…three paragraphs…</script></md>
</pd-collapse>
```

Note — automatic Plan-tab file mirror: when a pd-files tree lives on a
different tab from the phase controls (the usual Solution → Plan split), a
synced read-only copy is auto-injected next to the pd-dag/pd-stepper so the
click-through is visible in one place. Nothing to author.

Note — automatic plan lint: the doc checks its own consistency from the
structured attributes (files in the tree no phase touches, files a phase touches
that are missing from the tree, depends-on pointing at a missing phase, and
dependency cycles). Findings show in a panel at the top and are queued as a
single pending "lint" comment, so they ride the "Copy for agent" export to the
agent. Resolve them by fixing the attributes — clean plans show no panel. The
headless linter additionally reports any open pd-question (code "open-question",
non-zero exit) as a human gate — surface those to the user, don't "fix" them.

### <pd-decision id title status by date summary>
An authored architectural decision record (ADR). Use it for a call you (the
agent) or the author made directly — stating the decision, its rationale, the
alternatives weighed, and the consequences — when there was no review thread to
resolve. This is the home for decisions that aren't dictated by the requirements
or an existing repo pattern. status: accepted (default) | proposed | superseded.
by: who made the call (e.g. "agent"). summary: optional one-liner surfaced in
the pd-decisions log. Place each one directly after the section it concerns and
give it a stable id (e.g. "D-1") so threads and links can anchor to it.

A pd-decision differs from a pd-thread: a thread is an append-only review
conversation that becomes a decision once resolved; a pd-decision records a
settled call with no round-trip. Both feed the pd-decisions log.

```html
<pd-decision id="D-1" title="Token bucket over sliding window" status="accepted" by="agent"
  summary="Token bucket: simpler, bursts within SLA.">
  <md><script type="text/plain">
**Context:** Cap per-client request rate without penalising short bursts.
**Decision:** Token bucket, one Redis key per client.
**Alternatives:** Sliding-window log (more memory, exact); fixed-window (boundary bursts).
**Consequences:** Redis on the hot path; key eviction policy still open.
  </script></md>
</pd-decision>
```

### <pd-decisions title>
Auto-generated decision log: lists every pd-decision and every
resolved/rejected thread in the doc, in source order, with each one's outcome
(a pd-decision's summary, or a thread's last comment). Place once, usually in
the first tab. No children needed.

```html
<pd-decisions></pd-decisions>
```

### <pd-wire label h> / <pd-note>
Wireframe primitives for mockup sections. pd-wire is a labeled placeholder box
(h = min-height, e.g. "8rem"); pd-note is an annotation callout. Combine with
freeform Tailwind HTML for layout (grids, flex rows).

```html
<div class="grid grid-cols-3 gap-2">
  <pd-wire label="Nav" h="14rem"></pd-wire>
  <div class="col-span-2">
    <pd-wire label="Settings form" h="10rem"></pd-wire>
    <pd-wire label="Save / Cancel" h="3rem"></pd-wire>
  </div>
</div>
<pd-note>Form fields mirror the team config schema; nav reuses the app shell.</pd-note>
```

## Merging reviewer comments

Reviewers queue comments in the browser and paste an export block to you.
The block contains inline instructions — follow them exactly. Example:

```
=== DOC COMMENTS ===
doc: 021: API rate limiting

INSTRUCTIONS — you MUST follow these steps in order:
1. Merge every item below into the HTML doc file FIRST, before responding.
   - REPLY → append <pd-comment by="review">…</pd-comment> to the named thread.
   - NEW → create a <pd-thread anchor="…" priority="…" title="…"> after the anchored element, containing the comment.
   - ANSWER → append <pd-answer by="review">…</pd-answer> to the named pd-question and set its status="answered".
2. Then respond to each comment in the same thread (append your own <pd-comment by="author">).
   Set status="resolved" when addressed, or "rejected" with reasoning. Never edit or delete existing comments or answers.

[1] REPLY to thread "Why not sliding window?" (anchor: approach)
    Fine, but document the burst size limit.
[2] NEW p1 comment on "Files" (anchor: files)
    The limiter must also cover the websocket gateway.
[3] ANSWER to question "Which tier do internal services use?" (anchor: Q-1)
    Separate unlimited tier; key by service identity.
=== END DOC COMMENTS ===
```

After merging, tell the user; their browser copy clears pending comments via
the Clear button (localStorage — a reload after your edit shows merged state).
